# Generate a disposable OAM test database

The files `assets.jsonl`, `relations.jsonl` and `properties.jsonl` contain synthetic OAM entities and directed relationships. The logical IDs in these fixtures stay stable; the actual entity/edge IDs are generated by each database.

**Never run the seeder against an existing Amass installation or customer data.** The seeder validates the full fixture before writing, but database operations are not transactional and could be partially applied if an error occurs.

## SQLite

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/amass-ai-seed
# The target .db file must NOT exist.
go run ./cmd/ai-fixture-seed \
  -fixture ./testdata/ai \
  -sqlite /tmp/amass-ai-seed/fixture.db \
  -confirm-disposable
```

The CLI refuses existing SQLite files and refuses a path containing `asset.db`. Use only a disposable location. It does not remove the file afterwards; remove the entire disposable directory yourself when finished.

## PostgreSQL

Provision an EMPTY disposable database in a development PostgreSQL instance; the name MUST begin `amass_ai_fixture_`.

```bash
export AMASS_AI_FIXTURE_DSN='postgres://testuser:...@localhost:5432/amass_ai_fixture_01'
go run ./cmd/ai-fixture-seed -fixture ./testdata/ai \
  -postgres-dsn "$AMASS_AI_FIXTURE_DSN" -confirm-disposable
```

The name prefix is a safety guard, not a proof that the database is empty. Confirm manually that the database is disposable and unused. Do not pass production database URLs. Do not commit DSNs or credentials. Use CI to create and destroy the test database automatically.

## Test coverage

```bash
go test ./internal/aitestfixture/...
```

The integration test opens a brand-new SQLite database in `t.TempDir()` and validates two subsidiary edges and two independent source properties. PostgreSQL integration is supported by the same seeding function; a container-backed PostgreSQL test is still planned.
